judge_assessment.explanation: The judge's mathematics is right and I checked all of it against the artifacts: sqrt(72)=6sqrt(2); 5sqrt(3)+2sqrt(3)-sqrt(3)=6sqrt(3); sqrt(8)+sqrt(18)=2sqrt(2)+3sqrt(2)=5sqrt(2)=7.0711 -> 7.07 against sqrt(26)=5.0990 -> 5.10; sqrt(9)+sqrt(16)=7 while sqrt(25)=5; 4sqrt(5)+3sqrt(2)=13.1874 -> 13.19 against 7sqrt(7)=18.52; sqrt(12)+sqrt(27)-sqrt(3)=4sqrt(3)=6.9282 -> 6.93 against sqrt(36)=6; sqrt(2)+sqrt(8)=4.2426 -> 4.24 > sqrt(10)=3.1623. The planted errors do cleanly separate the product rule from the invented sum rule, as claimed. But 'exactly eight readable misconception-analysis problems are present' is where the judge stopped, and two coverage defects are visible in the same two files. First, problem 7 prints THREE response slots - the decimal value, the comparison symbol, and 'write sqrt(2) + sqrt(8) in simplest radical form' - and verify.json id 7 has only an approx (4.24) and a compare ('>'). The third answer, 3sqrt(2), appears in answer_key.tex as running prose ('so the sum is sqrt(2) + 2sqrt(2) = 3sqrt(2)') with no \ans box and no verify entry, even though an equiv entry would check it exactly the way ids 1, 2, 3 and 6 are checked. Second, the Quick Answers bank on page 1 reads '4. 7, -' and '7. 4.24, -' for two relations that gate_log.txt records as PASS, immediately above '8. -' which is a genuine manual item. That is the confirmed pathology in its sharpest form: in one printed column the same glyph means 'verified >' twice and 'nobody checked this' once, and nothing on the page tells the grader which is which. Problems 3, 4 and 5 also each print an explanation slot ('say in one line why the answer is not sqrt(26)', 'name the rule the student invented', 'explain what was added that should not have been') with no manual entry - only problem 8 is manual.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 4 is the best-chosen item on the sheet: sqrt(9) + sqrt(16) = 7 versus sqrt(25) = 5 uses only perfect squares, so the counterexample needs no decimals at all, and the key says why that matters ('A student who believes the rule can be asked to explain where the missing 2 went'). It also pre-empts the escape hatch that the rule 'only fails for ugly numbers'.

Problem 6's trap is declared as data, not prose: verify.json id 6 carries {desc: 'added and subtracted the radicands under one root, writing sqrt(36)', expr: 'sqrt(36)', value: 6}, and the key then explains why 6 versus 6.93 is a dangerous near miss that a student who only estimates will not notice. The distractor in the key and the machine-checked wrong value cannot drift apart.

Problem 7 is the only item where the two radicals genuinely do combine, and the key uses it to make a point the topic usually leaves out: the sum can be written as one radical, but the radicand is 18, not the 10 a student expects. That single line separates 'roots never add' from the real rule.

Problem 8's manual entry carries a real reviewer rubric in verify.json rather than a placeholder - it names the three things full credit needs (identical radicands AFTER simplifying as the condition, a counterexample with the arithmetic carried out, and no claim that the rule fails only for non-perfect squares), and the key repeats the same three criteria under 'What a reviewer should look for'.

root_causes.description: Verification was planned per problem rather than per printed response slot. Where a find-and-fix item asks for several things at once, the numeric slots were declared and the symbolic or verbal ones were not, even when the symbolic one is exactly as checkable as the numeric one (problem 7's simplest radical form is an equiv entry away). The gate chain reports 12/12 checks passed because it only asks whether declared entries verify.
evidence: worksheet.tex problem 7 asks for the decimal 'to two places', the 'correct comparison symbol', and 'sqrt(2) + sqrt(8) in simplest radical form'; verify.json id 7 has exactly two entries, approx 4.24 and compare '>'.
answer_key.tex problem 7 prints 3sqrt(2) only in prose, unboxed, so even check_answer_key.py's per-problem binding cannot see it.
worksheet.tex problems 3, 4 and 5 each print an explanation slot; the only manual entry in verify.json is id 8.

root_causes.description: The Quick Answers bank overloads one glyph. render_quick_answers._fmt returns '---' both when sympify cannot resolve a string (a relation) and when an id is manual-only, so on this sheet the grader sees '4. 7, -', '7. 4.24, -' and '8. -' with no way to tell a verified comparison from an unreviewed open response.
evidence: gate_log.txt records PASS for the compare entries of ids 4 and 7; verify.json id 8 is type manual with no expected value.
scripts/render_quick_answers.py docstring lines 22-25 assign '---' to both meanings ('if sympify fails the entry falls back to "---"' and 'manual-only ids print "---"').

improvements.title: Declare an equiv entry for problem 7's simplest-radical-form slot and gate multi-request problem stems
improvements.proposed_change: Build a response-slot inventory from the worksheet source before rendering: split each problem stem on its conjoined imperatives ('give the decimal value ... , write the correct comparison symbol ... , and write ... in simplest radical form') and require every slot to bind either to a verify entry whose expected value IS that response or to a manual entry naming it. For this case that means adding {id: 7, type: equiv, expr: 'sqrt(2) + sqrt(8)', expected: '3*sqrt(2)'} and boxing 3sqrt(2) with \ans in the key. Fail the build when a slot is unbound rather than reporting 'quick-answers PASS'.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture: this task's problem 7 stem plus a verify.json id 7 holding only the approx and compare entries. The slot check must exit non-zero naming the uncovered 'simplest radical form' slot. Adding the equiv entry expected '3*sqrt(2)' makes the fixture pass, and the rendered bank row for id 7 must then contain 3sqrt(2) as well as 4.24.
improvements.expected_impact: Closes the coverage hole on the one item of this sheet where the sum genuinely simplifies - the pedagogical punchline of the whole worksheet - and generalises to every multi-request find-and-fix stem, which is the dominant shape in misconception-analysis mode.
improvements.risk: Stem splitting on conjunctions will over-generate slots for work-shown phrases ('show the simplified form of each radical before you combine anything'); those must be allowed to bind to the same entry as the final answer or the manual count will inflate.

improvements.title: Require manual entries for the 'name the rule' and 'say in one line why' slots in problems 3, 4 and 5
improvements.proposed_change: Scan each worksheet problem block for open-response imperatives and fail the build unless that id carries a manual entry. Here that adds manual entries to ids 3 ('why the answer is not sqrt(26)'), 4 ('name the rule the student invented') and 5 ('explain what was added that should not have been'), each alongside the existing numeric checks, so the mixed machine-plus-manual problem becomes the normal declared shape for error analysis. State in SKILL.md that a numeric check on the same id never discharges an explanation slot.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture with problem 4's stem ('Compute the left side correctly, state which of the two values is greater, and name the rule the student invented') and verify.json id 4 holding only the eval 7 and the compare '>'. The check must exit non-zero naming the 'name the rule' slot; adding a manual entry for id 4 makes it pass and raises the run exit code to 2.
improvements.expected_impact: On a misconception sheet the naming of the error IS the learning objective; declaring it manual puts it in front of a human reviewer instead of letting a decimal stand in for a diagnosis.
improvements.risk: Three more manual items on an eight-problem sheet is a visible increase in review load; the manual-review aid in references/manual-review-aid.md should be recommended in the same breath so the load stays practical.

improvements.title: Print the verified relations for problems 4 and 7 instead of the glyph used for manual problem 8
improvements.proposed_change: Special-case relation strings in render_quick_answers._fmt before sympify, rendering the operator between the entry's compared values, and reserve '---' exclusively for ids whose entries are all manual. This sheet is the clearest demonstration that the two meanings must be separated: rows 4, 7 and 8 currently print the same glyph for three different situations.
improvements.regression_test: Render this task's verify.json and assert rows 4 and 7 contain a relation while row 8 is '---'. Today all three rows carry the em-dash, so the assertion fails before the fix and passes after.
improvements.expected_impact: A grader can tell the two comparison answers from the one open response on a page where all three currently look identical.
improvements.risk: Rendering '7 > 5' next to '13.19' lengthens rows and may cost a column in the bank layout; column_count already adapts, so the risk is cosmetic.

case_summary: A tightly focused radical error-analysis packet whose mathematics I re-derived in full and found correct, and whose design choices are worth keeping: problem 4's perfect-square counterexample needs no decimals, problem 6's near miss (6 versus 6.93) is declared as machine-checked trap data, problem 7 is the one case where the radicals really do combine and the key uses it to show the radicand is 18 rather than 10, and problem 8's manual entry carries a genuine three-point rubric. Two defects the judge did not reach. Problem 7 prints three response slots and verify.json covers two - the simplest radical form 3sqrt(2) sits unboxed in key prose with no equiv entry, although it is exactly as checkable as ids 1, 2, 3 and 6. And the Quick Answers bank prints '4. 7, -', '7. 4.24, -' and '8. -' in one column, where the first two dashes are verified relations and the third is the sheet's only manual item. Problems 3, 4 and 5 also carry explanation slots with no manual entry.
